statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk of 20% sits at the lower edge of the watch band, five points below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is WATCH. The evidence-based danger window runs from the 12:30Z September employment report through 15:00Z, covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ retraces 65-73 points off a corroborated 31,035 high as hourly extension reverses two hours before the September payrolls print
body: NQ futures trade 30,962.25 (+201.75, +0.66%) on a delayed CME quote timed 10:20:24Z, inside an overnight range of 30,760.25-31,035.25 against a 30,760.50 prior settlement on about 84.5k contracts. An independent delayed feed read 30,970.50 (+210.00, +0.68%) ten minutes earlier and put the session high at 31,035.50, so the extreme is corroborated rather than single-sourced. The decisive change this hour is a genuine retracement: price sat 8-16 points under the high in the 09:00Z hour and now sits roughly 65-73 points under it, about 0.23% off the extreme. Holding near the extreme was the one live Tail amplifier in the previous assessment, and it is no longer present. Extension first stalled, with the high advancing only 3.75 points in the 09:00Z hour against roughly 88 points in the hour before, and has now reversed into a pullback that was not shallow and did not fail. That is the opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement structure Tail is defined to measure, so Tail eases to the lower edge of the watch band at 20%. Cross-asset evidence remains unaligned with a one-way equity path. VIX is 16.03, down 2.20% from a 16.39 close, inside a 15.89-16.24 band. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.240% against a 5.238% prior close in a 5.223-5.262 range, and the 2-year is 4.793% against 4.787% in a 4.775-4.804 band; both have ticked marginally higher this hour, which is a mild conflict with the equity advance rather than an amplifier, and both sit well below Thursday's 5.342% 10-year print, the highest since April 2002. WTI crude is 89.59, down 3.53%, unwinding part of the Strait-of-Hormuz-driven spike after the EU energy commissioner said a strategic reserve release is possible under U.S. pressure; Brent has stabilised near 102. The dominant mode is recorded as mixed rather than trend-up: the day's +0.66% advance is intact and price still holds about 73% of the session range, but extension has reversed and the cross-asset set now points two ways. The September employment report lands at 12:30Z, roughly two hours after this assessment, with consensus near 85,000 payrolls against August's 162,000, the jobless rate seen holding at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.3% month-over-month and about 3.2% year-over-year. Nothing has printed. Under the current contract an unprinted release is a checkpoint, not an observed path, so its importance raises Stress to 76% in the high band and holds Confidence at 88% rather than lifting Tail. Confidence rests on two corroborating NQ feeds that agree on the session high, real-time 2-year and 10-year yields, a live VIX quote, a verified crude level, a published consensus for the release and a seven-day U.S. calendar whose FOMC minutes date was confirmed against the Federal Reserve's own meeting calendar. The one completeness gap is the shared Finviz context file, whose latest publication is dated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with a partial collection status; at roughly three days old it is well outside the 90-minute freshness limit and was therefore excluded from this assessment, which rests entirely on independent current research. The evidence-based danger window runs from the 12:30Z release through 15:00Z, covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. The forecast reaches the 25% block threshold only inside that window and only conditionally.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band. Tail opened the window at 20% in the 10:00Z hour on 1 October, peaked at 24% during the 14:00Z hour as the long-end selloff intensified, then printed 20% for thirteen consecutive hours through the Asian session before stepping to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. Stress ranged from 74% to a 79% overnight peak and finished the window at 75%; Confidence stayed between 87% and 89% throughout. Only the 08:00Z and 09:00Z slots were published as trend-up; every other hour in the window was mixed.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 20% for the current hour on the observed retracement, steps to 21% in the final pre-release hour as depth thins, and 24% in the 12:00Z hour containing the 12:30Z employment report. It reaches the 25% block threshold only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, pullbacks that fail and a long-end break back above Thursday's 5.342% peak; it is not an assertion that such a path has formed, and a confirmed retracement inside those hours would invalidate it. Tail then eases through the afternoon as repricing is assumed to complete, reaching the 20% floor at the 20:00Z cash close. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% across the release and open, then decays to a carried 60% once CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00Z. The final twelve slots sit inside that halt, where no price path can form; they publish a carried floor with Confidence stepping down to 74% to mark their distance from the live evidence cutoff rather than a projected structure.
